en: This reflection on the two different forms of anachronism now allows us to formulate a detailed and sharp-pointed thesis that will not be blunted by too many nuances. More than a thesis, it is a guide-to-thought with which we can mount an offensive against certain theories and emotional inclinations that postulate the completion or collapse of the process of history.
zh: 以上对两种时代错置的思考，使我们现在能够提出一个详尽、锋利，并且不会因过多限定而失去锋芒的命题。与其说它是命题，不如说它是一条思想指南；借助它，我们可以向那些设定历史进程已经完成或崩溃的理论和情感倾向发动进攻。

en: The feeling of déjà vu, awakened by ‘false recognition’, leads us to believe that even if we are faced with continuous change, everything is the same, everything is repeating itself. It goes without saying, however, that there would be no ‘false recognition’ if it were not for ‘the memory of the present’. Only where the virtual is in full flower right next to the actual could we ever illusorily confuse it for something that we have experienced already. The real anachronism makes use of materials that the formal anachronism puts at its disposal: and nothing else beyond them. As such, it uses its opposite as its own lever. But since ‘false recognition’ conceals the genesis of historical time, the genesis that the ‘memory of the present’, conversely, reveals and displays, to state that the former presupposes the latter has a consequence of some significance (here accorded the value of a ‘thesis’). Namely:

children: the ‘end of history’ is an idea, or state of mind, that arises precisely when the very condition of possibility of history comes into view

en: ; when the root of all historical activity is cast out onto the surface of historical becoming, and is evident as a phenomenon; when the
of experience is itself also manifested
zh: 由“错误再认”唤起的既视感，使我们相信：即便面对持续不断的变化，一切仍然相同，一切都在重复。然而，不言而喻，如果没有“对当下的记忆”，也就不会有“错误再认”。唯有潜在态在现实态近旁充分绽放，我们才可能产生幻觉，把前者误认成自己已经经历过的东西。现实的时代错置所使用的，只是形式的时代错置交到它手中的材料，除此以外别无他物；因此，它以自己的对立面作为杠杆。然而，“错误再认”遮蔽了历史时间的生成，而“对当下的记忆”反过来揭示并展示这种生成。因此，断言前者以后一者为前提，会引出一个相当重要的结论——在这里，这一结论获得“命题”的价值。也就是说：“历史的终结”这一观念或心境，恰恰在历史自身的可能性条件进入视野时出现；恰恰在一切历史活动的根部被抛到历史生成的表面，并作为现象清楚显现时出现；恰恰在经验的历史性自身也历史性地显现时出现。

en: The best way to examine this guide-to-thought more closely is to put it to the test. That is, we ought to test the
waters of its explanatory capacity and critical force in relation to an example text. In a long footnote to his

children: Introduction à la lecture de Hegel

en: , Alexandre Kojève maintains that the exhaustion of history diagnosed by Hegel is no longer, in our epoch, some future eventuality, but rather is a

The industrial societies of the post-Second World War period, in this view, had now left behind the struggle against nature and the struggle for mutual recognition. Labour – that is, the opposition between Subject and Object – was losing weight and significance as automated production processes captured and subjugated nature in such measure as to allow for a stable relation with it. Similarly, politics – the search for the recognition of others by way of wars and revolutions – was also declining. The bloody conflicts of the last century represented only a ‘spatial extension’ of the essential results achieved once and for all time by Robespierre and Napoleon. Also disappearing together with Labour and Politics is ‘Action in the strong sense of the term’, which, rejecting ‘the given’, was always seeking to establish a historically new world. But what forms of life prevail in post-historical societies? Kojève saw two of them, a pair that diverged and were even opposites.
zh: 更仔细地考察这条思想指南，最好的办法是让它接受检验。也就是说，我们应当选取一篇范例文本，试探它的解释能力和批判力量。亚历山大·科耶夫在《黑格尔导读》的一篇长脚注中主张：黑格尔所诊断的历史耗尽，在我们的时代已不再是未来可能发生之事，而是既成事实（fait accompli）。

按照这种看法，第二次世界大战后的工业社会已经把同自然的斗争和争取相互承认的斗争抛在身后。劳动——也就是主体与客体的对立——正在失去分量和意义，因为自动化生产过程已经在如此大的程度上捕获并征服自然，以至人们能够同自然建立稳定关系。政治——借助战争和革命寻求他人承认——也同样在衰退。上个世纪的血腥冲突，不过是罗伯斯庇尔和拿破仑一劳永逸取得的根本成果在“空间上的扩展”。随着劳动和政治一同消失的，还有“严格意义上的行动”；这种行动拒绝“既定之物”，始终谋求建立一个历史上崭新的世界。那么，在后历史社会中占据支配地位的是什么生活形式？科耶夫辨认出两种彼此分歧、甚至相互对立的形式。

en: On the one hand, the post-history in which we are supposedly immersed is explained as man ‘becoming an animal again’. Rather than inhabiting a
with struggle and labour, the living being of the
species is now encapsulated in an
, to which it adapts without any kind of friction. Certainly, even

after the conclusion of the business of History, we will build houses and create works of art, but following the same impulse that leads a bird to make its nest or a spider to spin its web. Nothing like happiness is any longer in question: rather, ‘men will surely be
as a result of their
and playful behavior inasmuch as, by definition, they will be contented with it’. Also accounted for here is the ‘definitive disappearance of human discourse (

) in the strict sense’. In its place, ‘vocal signals or sign “language” ’ will proliferate, to which we would react by conditioned reflex: nothing much different from ‘what is supposed to be the “language” of bees’. In Kojève’s view, the
, in which the eternal present typical of an ‘environment’ dominates, exemplifies well the condition of post-historical animals.
zh: 一方面，据说我们已经沉浸其中的后历史，被解释为人“重新变成动物”。智人这个物种的生命体不再栖居于一个充满斗争和劳动的世界，而是被封闭在一个环境之中，并毫无摩擦地适应它。即使历史事务已经结束，我们当然仍会建造房屋、创作艺术品，但那将出于鸟筑巢或蜘蛛结网的同一种冲动。此时涉及的已不再是任何近似幸福的东西；相反，“人们无疑会因自己的艺术、性爱和游戏行为而感到满足，因为按照定义，他们将以这些行为为满足”。这里还包括“严格意义上的人类话语（逻各斯，Logos）的彻底消失”。取而代之而大量增殖的是“声音信号或手势‘语言’”；我们会以条件反射作出回应，它们同所谓蜜蜂的“语言”没有太大差别。在科耶夫看来，由“环境”所特有的永恒当下支配的美国生活方式，很好地体现了后历史动物的处境。

en: Another way of being also comes into view at the end of history, diametrically opposed to the one just sketched out. It is a matter of

. That is to say, an affected attitude that shrinks from any utilitarian automatism and clashes with the ‘ “animal” or “natural” given’. Though having nothing to do with Labour or ‘warlike and revolutionary Fights’, the snob nonetheless maintains a separation between the
and

of his own activity, such as to guarantee the former a marked independence from (and supremacy over) the latter. The unequalled model of this way of being is Japanese culture: there, indeed, Noh theatre, the tea ceremony, and the art of flower arranging, have built up a widespread propensity to ‘live according to totally formalized values’. No longer historical yet still human (the fracture between Subject and Object having been reinvented), Japanese snobbery, according to Kojève, alludes to a principle-hope of general applicability: ‘While henceforth speaking
in an
fashion of everything that is given to him, post-historical Man must continue to
“form” from “content”, doing so no longer in order actively to transform the latter, but so that he may
himself as a pure “form” to himself and to others taken as “content” of any sort.’
zh: 历史终结处还显现出另一种存在方式，它与刚才勾勒的存在方式截然相反。这就是势利主义（snobbery），也就是一种拒斥一切功利性自动机制、同“‘动物性的’或‘自然的’既定之物”发生冲突的矫饰姿态。势利者虽然与劳动或“战争和革命的斗争”无关，却仍然维持自己活动的形式与内容之间的分离，从而保证前者相对于后者具有显著的独立性和优越地位。这种存在方式无与伦比的范型是日本文化：在那里，能剧、茶道和花道培养出一种普遍倾向，使人“依照完全形式化的价值生活”。科耶夫认为，日本的势利主义不再属于历史却仍具人性（因为主体与客体之间的裂缝得到了重新发明）；它暗示了一个可以普遍适用的希望原则：“后历史的人从此以后虽然必须以适当方式谈论给予他的一切，却仍须继续把‘形式’同‘内容’分离；这样做不再是为了主动改造后者，而是为了使他能够以纯粹‘形式’的身份，同作为任意一种‘内容’的自己和他人相对立。”

en: Becoming an animal again, or else snobbery. The alternative proposed by Kojève is in many aspects akin to that with which we dealt in the previous few pages: real anachronism or formal anachronism, false recognition or memory of the present. However, in order to make clear this consonance, we must call into question the conceptual schema within which Kojève inscribes his pair of opposed choices. And it attracts two principal objections.
zh: 重新变成动物，或者势利主义。科耶夫提出的这个二选一，在许多方面近似于我们前几页讨论的二选一：现实的时代错置或形式的时代错置，错误再认或对当下的记忆。不过，为了阐明这种呼应，我们必须质疑科耶夫用来容纳这对相反选择的概念图式。它引出了两项主要反对意见。

en: First off, far from it playing a protagonist’s role on the little stage of post-history, we could even say that snobbery constitutes the very quintessence of historical life. Its prerogative is to show the autonomy and exuberance of ‘forms’ with respect to ‘contents’: but what are this autonomy and exuberance, other than the

of Labour and Politics: in other words, ‘Action in the strong sense of the term’? Snobbery unveils the foundation of historical conflicts, since it devotes itself to representing, through a series of determinate acts, the contrast that generally exists between human action and ‘the given’. Detaching ‘forms’ from ‘contents’, snobbery
expresses the impossibility of any

entirely realising the corresponding capacity-to-do. To put it another way: snobbery is a peculiar praxis that reflects in itself – and relentlessly exhibits – the historicity of every type of praxis (including ‘snobbish’ praxis as well, of course). To attribute a post-historical character to the snob is a classic case of being blinded by too much light.
zh: 首先，势利主义远非后历史小舞台上的主角；我们甚至可以说，它构成了历史生活的精髓。它的特性是展示“形式”相对于“内容”的自主性和充盈：然而，这种自主性和充盈若不是劳动与政治——换句话说，“严格意义上的行动”——的先决条件，又能是什么？势利主义揭开了历史冲突的基础，因为它致力于通过一系列具体实现，表现人类行动与“既定之物”之间普遍存在的对立。势利主义把“形式”同“内容”分离，事实上表达了任何事实都不可能完全实现与它相应的行动能力。换一种说法：势利主义是一种特殊实践（praxis），它在自身中反映并不停展示每一种实践——当然也包括“势利的”实践——所具有的历史性。把后历史性质归给势利者，是被过强的光线晃瞎眼睛的典型事例。

en: Secondly, ‘becoming an animal again’ is not a biological fate, corresponding to the disappearance of any friction with nature. On the contrary, it is an existential possibility that reveals itself in so far as the gap with ‘the given’ is exaggeratedly accentuated, becomes most visible, and is experienced

. But this accentuation, as well as the visibility and direct experience of the gap with ‘the given’, is the result of snobbery. As such, we must say that ‘becoming an animal again’ is the existential possibility that reveals itself on the basis of the full affirmation of the snobbish lifestyle. For Kojève, the post-historical animal always adheres symbiotically to the ‘contents’ of its action, while the snob distances himself from them, counterposing to this the autonomy of ‘forms’. But he is mistaken here. Such a symbiotic adherence would only be conceivable, in truth, if we supposed that

somersaulted into the immutable condition of the wolf or the ape; but if we did suppose such a somersault, the self-distancing subsequently operated by the snob would itself be inconceivable. On closer inspection, the fracture between the ‘forms’ and ‘contents’ of activity is at the basis of

modes of being. The division that separates and renders them antithetical is, rather, the following: the snob tries to live at the level of this fracture, understanding that the source of history is to be found within it; the post-historical animal, conversely, makes the overpopulation of forms into an
at one remove, viscous and all-embracing, and

to its prescriptions in virtue of some (pseudo-)instinctive behaviour. To use Kojève’s example: the post-historical animal is he who reduces the most elaborate, affected aspects of the tea ceremony to an immediate ‘given’. Precisely because they are detached from their natural ‘contents’, and precisely

because of their independence (and hypertrophy), ‘forms’ are surreptitiously taken for a catalogue of minute ‘contents’ – and with this, their frictionless mutual penetration does indeed seem possible.
zh: 其次，“重新变成动物”并不是一种对应于同自然之间一切摩擦消失的生物学命运。相反，它是一种生存可能性：当我们同“既定之物”的裂隙被过度凸显、变得最为可见，并且作为裂隙本身被直接经验时，这种可能性才会显露。然而，对裂隙的这种凸显，以及裂隙的可见和直接经验，正是势利主义的结果。因此，我们必须说，“重新变成动物”是在势利生活方式得到充分肯定的基础上显露出来的一种生存可能性。在科耶夫笔下，后历史动物总是与自己行动的“内容”共生地黏合在一起；势利者则同内容拉开距离，并以“形式”的自主性与之相对。但他在这里错了。严格说来，只有假定智人翻着筋斗跌进狼或猿那种恒定不变的处境，这种共生黏合才可以设想；可是一旦作出这种假定，势利者随后实行的自我疏离本身又变得不可设想。仔细看来，活动的“形式”与“内容”之间的断裂，是两种存在方式共同的基础。真正把它们分开并使之彼此对立的，是下面这一点：势利者试图在断裂本身的层次上生活，明白历史的源头就在其中；后历史动物则把过度繁殖的形式变成一个衍生的、黏稠而无所不包的环境，并凭借某种（伪）本能行为适应其规定。沿用科耶夫的例子：后历史动物就是把茶道中最精巧、最矫饰的面向还原成直接“既定之物”的人。“形式”恰恰因为脱离其自然“内容”，也恰恰因为其独立性（及过度膨胀），才被暗中当成一份细小“内容”的目录；这样一来，它们彼此间毫无摩擦的渗透看起来确实成为可能。

en: The post-historical animal and the snob do not limit themselves to coexisting spatially, each of them extraneous and refractory with regard to the other. Within the latter we can still make out the silhouette of the former, even if it has been disfigured and upended. The intimate relationship between these two contenders does not, however, blunt the contest itself. The antithesis between these two forms of life is all the more radical, indeed, the more they are based on identical premises and defined against the same background. This background is not, as Kojève supposes, the ‘end of history’. On the contrary, the opposition between ‘becoming an animal again’ and snobbery is resolved on the stage of a
epoch: the epoch in which, let us repeat, not only do we experience historical events, but we face up to the very thing that confers a historical tone on every event.
zh: 后历史动物与势利者并不只是并存于空间之中，彼此陌生而互不相容。我们仍能在后者内部辨认出前者的轮廓，尽管它已经变形并被颠倒。这两个对手之间的内在关系并没有削弱争执本身。恰恰相反，这两种生活形式越是建立在相同前提上、越是在同一个背景中得到界定，二者的对立就越彻底。这个背景并不是科耶夫所假定的“历史终结”。相反，“重新变成动物”与势利主义之间的对抗，是在一个历史性高度凸显的时代（hyper-historical epoch）的舞台上得到解决的；再说一遍，在这个时代，我们不仅经历历史事件，而且直面那个赋予每个事件以历史色调的东西本身。

children: The memory of the present is a very snobbish thing indeed

en: . And the converse is also true: snobbery is, in its essentials, the memory of the present. By applying the past-in-general to a current event, we subvert the ‘ “natural” or “animal” given’, thus interrupting the automatism of the action that is underway. The formal anachronism is constantly
anew. The snobbery of memory splits the univocal

into two heterogeneous sides. It sets a potential (remembered) present alongside the real (perceived) present: but, even while placing them together, it simultaneously underlines their incommensurability and the discrepancy between them. It is eminently snobbish to re-evoke the virtual

nature of language at the very moment in which a particular utterance is being uttered: and it is thus, indeed, that the ‘difference of nature’ between capacity-to-speak (faculty) and the word spoken (performance) becomes manifest. This difference is the marker of ‘human discourse (
) in the strict sense’. And this is confirmed in the perspicacious whispers of those who, finding a familiar word strange, place it in inverted commas (thus citing or
it) already as it is being employed in its instrumental guise.
zh: 对当下的记忆确实是一件极其势利的事情。反过来说也成立：势利主义在其本质上就是对当下的记忆。把一般过去应用于当前事件，我们便颠覆了“‘自然的’或‘动物性的’既定之物”，从而中断正在进行的行动之自动机制。形式的时代错置不断重新撤除环境。记忆的势利主义把意义单一的此时此地分裂成异质的两面。它把潜在的（被记住的）当下同实在的（被知觉的）当下并置；但就在把二者放到一起时，也同时突出它们不可通约及彼此偏离。恰恰在某个具体话语被说出之际，重新唤起语言的潜在性质，是最典型的势利姿态；正是在这一刻，言说能力（官能）与说出的词（表现）之间的“性质差别”才显现。这种差别是“严格意义上的人类话语（逻各斯）”的标志。那些把熟悉词语看成陌生之物的人所发出的敏锐低语证实了这一点：他们在工具性地使用一个词时，已经把它放进引号（从而引用或记住它）。

children: False recognition suits ‘becoming an animal again’ very well

en: . And the converse is also true: ‘becoming an animal again’ announces itself first and foremost as false recognition. When today’s potential is confused for an already-experienced act, which we are now constrained to copy unvaryingly, human praxis degenerates into repetitive, predetermined behaviour patterns. To identify the faculty (capacity-to-do) with a list of specific performances (

) carves out an environment for us within which any freedom from ‘the given’ is imperceptible. It is clear, however, that this confusion and this identification would be impossible if the potential and the faculty had not acquired an autonomous significance thanks to the snobbish memory of the present. When we experience language through the prism of each concrete utterance, communication resembles a weft of ‘vocal signals or sign “language” ’, but, in experiencing it, we take it for an immense reservoir of
-spoken words, to be repeated and repeated again in correspondence with environmental stimuli. The impulse for happiness declines, and people are simply content (inasmuch as they are
with their own behaviour), when the disposition to enjoy pleasure appears as such – as distinct from
a single actual pleasure – but, at the same time, it is equated (through ‘false recognition’, indeed) with the sum of
-enjoyed pleasures.
zh: “错误再认”非常适合“重新变成动物”。反过来说也成立：“重新变成动物”首先就是以错误再认的形式宣告自身。当今日的潜能被误认成已经经历过、而我们此刻不得不原样复制的实现时，人类实践便退化为重复而预定的行为模式。把官能（行动能力）等同于一份具体表现（既成事实）的清单，会为我们划出一个环境；在这个环境中，任何摆脱“既定之物”的自由都无法被感知。不过很清楚，如果潜能和官能没有借助势利的对当下记忆而取得自主意义，这种混淆和等同就不可能发生。当我们透过每一句具体话语体验语言，却又把它当成一个储存已说词语的巨大仓库、认为其中的词语只能随着环境刺激反复重述时，沟通便近似于由‘声音信号或手势“语言”’编织而成的网络。当享受快感的禀赋本身显现出来——与单个现实快感相区分——却又同时（恰恰通过“错误再认”）被等同于已经享受过的全部快感时，追求幸福的冲动便会衰退，人们只是感到满足（因为他们满足于自己的行为）。
Alexandre Kojève, Introduction to the Reading of Hegel, Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1980。正文只讨论其中的一篇长注；科耶夫在这篇注中展开了他1938—1939年在高等研究实践学院所作第十二次讲座中的讨论。
